fact: KeNIA's Kenya Innovation Outlook 2024 says the Startup Bill has been in parliamentary debate since 2021 and is not yet approved or enacted, and that the government missed its April 2024 enactment target.

The State Department for MSMEs Development posts the text of a Start-up Bill, 2024, which would make Kenya Industrial Estates the body that labels start-ups, incubators and accelerators and would provide tax reliefs and funds for start-ups; the text is a bill, not an enacted act.

The Startup Bill, 2022 (Senate Bills No. 14) was published in Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 207 of 30 December 2022 for introduction in the Senate, providing for a registrar of startups, certified incubators, an optional credit guarantee scheme and fiscal incentives.
The bill's memorandum of objects and reasons states that there is currently no regulatory framework for startups in Kenya.
